newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economic recovery becoming firmer - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan economic recovery becoming firmer - BOJ.

text.p: Japan's economy is continuing on a gradual recovery track and the strength of the recovery is becoming firmer, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Thursday.
He said the central bank's view on the economy had been generally supported by the BOJ's March "tankan" short-term survey released last week.

"The economy is continuing its gradual recovery and in this environment, the strength of the recovery is still gaining firmness. The result of the March tankan survey announced last week generally backs up this view," he said.

Matsushita, speaking at a conference of trust bankers, said it appeared that an increase in production was leading to higher company profits and household incomes. He said this has stimulated an increase in private sector demand and thus growth in production.
Matsushita said the tankan survey showed that this favourable economic mechanism was starting to function.
The survey showed improvements in supply and demand conditions for products, fixed investments and employment conditions, as well as a better outlook for corporate profits this fiscal year, he said.
"The economy will inevitably slow down temporarily around the summer in reaction to the rush (in purchases) before the consumption tax increase (on April 1, 1997)," he said.
"But looking at the recent strength in the cyclical (economic) mechanism, there is a high possibility that the trend of economic recovery will continue."

The governor said declines in prices have come to a halt on the back of a rise in prices of imported goods and better domestic demand and supply conditions. He said the BOJ would keep careful watch on price movements, although it does not expect further upward pressure from imports as crude oil prices have fallen.
"Our monetary policy for now is to continue putting emphasis on making the basis for economic recovery firmer, while keeping close watch over (economic) developments," he said.

Matsushita said it was important to address the issue of problem loans quickly. He said financial institutions are planning to post losses to dispose of problem loans and to come up with far-reaching restructuring plans. Some were deciding on mergers to strengthen their businesses, he said.
The governor said these moves were "meaningful" from the standpoint of overcoming problem loans quickly and of coping with upcoming financial reforms.
"We will give what support we can should financial institutions face liquidity problems in the process of their serious restructuring efforts," he said.
